paths.description: Homepage discovery and phone-finder entry point; represents global navigation, search, consent, popular/latest product modules. Not covering every repeated homepage card.
Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra detail page; represents product specifications and the primary research journey.
Smartphone category; represents catalog/listing and filtering templates. Other categories were omitted as template duplicates.
Samsung Galaxy M14 news article; represents editorial/content pages. Other news/review pages were omitted as template duplicates.
S23 Ultra versus S24 Ultra; represents the high-value comparison journey. Other pairs were omitted as template duplicates.
Deliberately invalid route to exercise HTTP failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The site remains light under a dark color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in page surfaces to the light/contrast captures, and the CSS probe found zero prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not handled and baseline contrast failures remain
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; Lighthouse failed color-contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations and correct baseline contrast ratios.

findings.summary: Navigation swaps are abrupt rather than using view transitions
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found zero view-transition usage across the representative MPA templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation cue
findings.evidence: Representative pages are 3,295 to 13,646px tall, while the CSS probe found no scroll-timeline or scroll-state technique.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress or responsive sticky-header state for long content pages.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page movement do not visibly guide attention
findings.evidence: The source probe found no View Transition, highlight, or scroll-marker technique on long product and comparison pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Cue destination changes with transitions, focus movement, or section highlighting.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent wall obscures every representative mobile page on load
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show a 323px-wide modal covering nearly the entire 360x800 viewport before users can read product, article, listing, or comparison content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where lawful, minimise initial choices, and preserve immediate access to content.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay is not exposed through native dialog/popover primitives
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements while screenshots show a modal interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal behavior with dialog and platform focus/dismiss semantics, or reduce it to a non-modal notice.

findings.summary: Dense borders and repeated cards compete with primary content
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show nearly every section and row boxed with borders while the consent layer adds further chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated borders and group related content with spacing and headings.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior relies on viewport rules rather than reusable component queries
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found zero @container rules across reused product-card, filter, and comparison components.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards and comparison modules that appear at different widths.

findings.summary: Touch targets and keyboard focus are inadequate
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size; the focus probe found visible controls as small as 32x32 and computed outline-style none on sampled links, buttons, inputs, and selects.
findings.suggestedFix: Make controls at least 44 CSS pixels where practical and define a strong :focus-visible style.

findings.summary: The primary browse flow is interrupted before it begins
findings.evidence: Every representative mobile route opens behind the same full-screen consent wall, adding a mandatory detour before product discovery or comparison.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow content browsing before consent and defer optional advertising choices until context requires them.

findings.summary: Mobile loading is slow
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.5s, FCP 2.9s, TTI 10.6s and performance 66; the raw trace measured LCP 3.78s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, shorten render-blocking chains, and defer non-critical third-party work.

findings.summary: Main-thread scripting blocks responsiveness during load
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 3 long tasks, a longest task of 175.65ms, and 283.3ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks and defer analytics/advertising scripts until idle or consent.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and cache inefficiencies delay content
findings.evidence: HAR found nine parser-inserted stylesheet candidates; Lighthouse estimated 770ms render-blocking savings and 585KiB cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, load the rest non-blockingly, self-host/subset fonts, and set useful cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused code
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 313KiB unused JavaScript and 39KiB unused CSS; HAR shows 15 scripts and 9 stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove page-irrelevant bundles and conditionally load feature and third-party scripts.

findings.summary: Core controls lack accessible names and labels
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name, label, select-name, aria-valid-attr-value, and list semantics; the probe also found unlabelled search/email/password inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic name, associate labels, repair ARIA values, and correct list markup.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast failed on the homepage under its mobile accessibility audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA and retest all states.

findings.summary: Heading order and focus visibility are not reliable
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order, while the focus probe reported outline-style none for sampled interactive controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sequential heading hierarchy and a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: Dense mobile text and controls reduce reading comfort
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show long consent copy in a narrow overlay and tightly packed card/specification layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase line-height and spacing, shorten consent copy, and use comfortable line lengths.

findings.summary: Small targets undermine touch and zoomed use
findings.evidence: Although all tested templates reflowed without horizontal overflow at 360px, Lighthouse failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target size and spacing while preserving the existing successful mobile reflow.

findings.summary: Image markup is poorly sized
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 68/69 images without both dimensions, 29 oversized images, 52 without srcset, and Lighthouse found incorrect aspect ratios.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height and responsive srcset/sizes from the image pipeline.

findings.summary: Chrome reports browser platform issues
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed inspector-issues even though console, BFCache, paste prevention, source maps, and prompt-on-load audits passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Review and resolve the exact DevTools Issues entries and keep the passing platform hygiene checks.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but headers and cookies are weak
findings.evidence: Header capture found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame policy, referrer policy, or permissions policy; all three cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a staged CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing protection, and secure appropriate SameSite cookie attributes.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising dominate the network footprint
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 30 third-party requests and 779,961 transferred bytes; tracker capture found 10 third-party origins and three known trackers.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential trackers behind consent, remove low-value vendors, and batch/minimise analytics.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and CSP all absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and an enforceable CSP.

findings.summary: The site registers service workers but is not installable and no offline fallback was demonstrated
findings.evidence: The platform probe found two service-worker registrations but no web app manifest.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid manifest and verify a useful offline fallback for previously visited content, or remove unnecessary registrations.

findings.summary: Locale-sensitive content is hard-coded for one locale
findings.evidence: Representative content renders prices as “TK.” and English date prose, with no locale selector or observed locale-aware alternative.
findings.suggestedFix: Format currency, numbers, and dates through Intl using an explicit Bangladesh locale and make locale strategy clear.

findings.summary: Sign-in and other text fields omit autofill assistance
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found email, password, text, and search inputs without appropriate autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Add purpose-specific autocomplete tokens such as email, current-password, username, and search where applicable.

findings.summary: Images are transferred at wasteful resolutions
findings.evidence: The image audit found 29 oversized images, 63 below-fold images without lazy loading, 52 without srcset, and 8 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive modern-format variants, lazy-load below-fold media, and preserve intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics create avoidable background work
findings.evidence: HAR shows 30 third-party requests while the trace records 283.3ms blocking time; major script bytes come from ad and analytics vendors.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay or remove non-essential vendor work and deprioritise background fetches.

findings.summary: Third parties consume more than half of transferred bytes
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 779,961 of 1,422,977 bytes, led by advertising, tag management, consent, and fonts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and load optional vendors only after consent and interaction.

taskList.title: Remove the blocking consent detour and defer optional vendors
Fix accessible names, labels, heading order, focus and target size
Improve LCP and delivery by deferring third parties and non-critical CSS
Deploy security headers and secure cookie attributes
Build a responsive image pipeline with dimensions, srcset and lazy loading
Reduce third-party byte and request budgets
Add input autocomplete and locale-aware formatting
